question.worked_solution:
Approaching from the left, we have $x<4,$ so we use the expression $g(x)=x-2.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}(x+2) \\  & =4+2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Approaching from the right, we have $x>4,$ so we use the expression $g(x)={e}^{x-4}+1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}(\,{e}^{x-4}+1\,) \\  & ={e}^{4-4}+1 \\  & ={e}^{0}+1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}g(x)=6,\,{lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}g(x)=2.
$$
